content.thinking:
I'm checking the root-cause claim against the evidence. The first half, that the new code changed what a summary cache entry holds, is supported by D1. The second half, that the new code wrote the entry, doesn't hold: F1 says nothing in this repository writes these entries, and the bare-id entry comes from an outside writer. That's what I need to sort out next.

I'm checking whether the root-cause claim that the new code wrote the bare-id entry actually holds. F1 says nothing in this repository writes these entries, so that part needs a closer look against what the logs show about where the old version reads.

I'm now checking whether the claim that the new code wrote the entries holds up. The logs show the stale entries are where the previous version reads, so the cache-sharing part is backed. Whether the failing replicas were actually on the old version still needs a closer look.

I'm going through the remaining claims against the evidence. The ruled-out list holds up: the metrics read back six hours before onset show the usual error rate, the account pages render normally after the change, and the rollback restored normal service. For the last chain, I'm checking that the replicas still on the previous version could not read the two-field entries.

I'm checking the remaining claims against the record. The "no check was seen" point holds, since nothing in the logs shows one. For the account-page claim, the earlier failure is clear from the ValueError in the logs, but I still need to confirm what the old reader does with an unreadable entry, since the docstring only covers misses and unreachable caches.

I'm working through the remaining points against the record. The rollout-health and ruled-out items hold up: the rollout kept both revisions serving until the rollback, and the reasoning about the fix only working with an outside change is backed by the evidence. Nobody being paged is a plain fact from the record, so I'll note it as is.

supported.quote: The new code changed what a summary cache entry holds, from a bare figure in cents to an 'amount/items' text, and wrote it where the previous version also reads, with no versioned key or other way to keep the two shapes apart.

Replicas still on the previous version share that cache during the paused rolling update, and their reader expects a bare cents figure, so it raised ValueError on the new entries and the account page request failed.

A software update changed the format the shop uses to save each shopper's spending summary, and the copies of the shop still running the previous version expected the old format, could not read the new entries, and failed the account page.
Deploying the same revision again, or any revision that writes the two-field cache entries, could make account pages fail again while replicas of the earlier revision are still serving.
Account pages failed for some shoppers
Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the share of the service's requests that failed rose well above its usual level.
Those requests failed because reading the shopper's summary cache entry in src/io_shop/summary_cache.py raised a ValueError: the entry was an 'amount/items' text, not a figure in cents.

Entries in that two-field shape came from revision 696c33a, deployed at {P2.1}. It changed a cache entry from a bare figure in cents to one text holding the figure and the number of purchases behind it.

The earlier deploy of revision 5470c1a (P1). The metrics read back over the hours after it show the service at its usual error rate until the onset, account pages logged as rendering normally after it, and the confirmed rollback left that revision running with the service back to normal.
The new shape broke pages because, as read at {T10.1}, the rolling update was paused with {T10.5} replicas still on revision 5470c1a, and those replicas could not read the two-field entries.

No check was seen that tested the change against the previous revision reading the same cache, such as a mixed-version compatibility test, before a change to the shape of a shared cache entry went out.

The previous revision's cache reader fails the account page when it meets an entry it cannot read, instead of treating the entry as a miss and working the figure out, which is what the module's own docstring says should happen.
No rollout health gate was seen that halts and rolls back an io-shop rolling update when errors rise. The rollout stayed in place, with both revisions serving, until Argus rolled it back.
The Code-Fix Agent kept none of the fix it wrote, once its reading showed the fix would help only together with a change outside the repository.
Nobody was paged: the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to any on-call incident.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.
